study_design: Retrospective case-control study of incident prostate cancer patients and age frequency-matched controls
cohort_total_n_excerpt: A sample of 652 participants (244 incident prostate cancer patients, aged 64-75 years, and 408 age frequency-matched controls) were recruited in Ho Chi Minh City during 2013-2015.
reason: This retrospective case-control study evaluates general incident prostate cancer. The abstract does not define or analyze an aggressive prostate cancer subtype.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: No statistically significant associations were found for the intake of α-carotene, β-carotene, β-cryptoxanthin, lutein, zeaxanthin, and major food sources of carotenoids.
estimate_classifications.reason: The abstract explicitly evaluates lutein intake in relation to general prostate cancer and reports no aggressive subtype analysis.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The risk of prostate cancer decreased with increasing intakes of lycopene, tomatoes, and carrots; the respective ORs (95% CIs) were 0.46 (0.27, 0.77), 0.39 (0.23, 0.66), and 0.35 (0.21, 0.58), when comparing the highest with the lowest tertile of intake (p for trend < 0.01).
estimate_classifications.reason: The tomato estimate is explicitly for general prostate cancer, with no aggressive subtype specified.
